Fed expected to keep rates in 2026 (TD Securities)

market_view: SPY is near highs but breadth is poor. Tech and semis are selling off while energy leads, and a supertanker was reportedly hit in Hormuz on Oct 12. Rate and inflation data are conflicting, with some hike risk and long yields elevated. I'm starting a fresh portfolio tilted toward energy momentum, software/quality and defensive health care. I'm holding SPY at 45%.

sources.title: Fed policymakers saw multiple 2026 rate hikes as likely, September FOMC minutes show
Federal Reserve: more hikes ahead after October pause - UOB
Kalshi traders bet on a hot September CPI print
Oil climbs as US-Iran strikes in Hormuz raise supply fears

market_view: The S&P 500 is flat and close to its highs. Volatility is very low (about 10% annualised on a 20-day basis), but participation is narrow: only 38% of our ETFs trade above their 50-day averages. Big-bank earnings (GS, JPM) are strong. Semis and Asian tech are still under pressure. The Iran conflict is still pushing up energy and inflation, and reports say Iran is preparing for possible US strikes after the midterms. Tomorrow's September CPI is expected to come in hot on the headline number because of fuel prices, with core near 2.4%. The Fed hiked in September and meets Oct 27-28. With that print one day away and the portfolio set up only yesterday, I'm keeping the current energy, software, health care and quality mix.
key_drivers: Oct 13: Goldman Sachs beat Q3 estimates, with equities trading revenue up 72%. JPM also reported. The Dow is up, the Nasdaq slightly down and oil lower intraday.

Oct 13: Reports that Iran is preparing for renewed war and fortifying nuclear sites, with the threat of US strikes after the midterms. This keeps a geopolitical premium in oil, which supports XLE and XOP.
Oct 14: September CPI. Consensus is about 3.6-3.7% year on year for the headline and about 2.4% for core. Kalshi puts roughly 90% odds on a month-over-month rise above 0.4%.
The Fed hiked in September to 3.75-4.00%. Weak September payrolls (+29k) have cut the odds of an October hike to about 17%. Waller and Hammack lean hawkish on yields.
Oct 12: The watcher added XLE and XLV on 5/6 signals. Both buys are protected for 3 trading days.

positions.thesis: Oil prices are driven by the Iran war. XLE has strong momentum, sits 17.6% above its 200-day average and is near 20-day highs. It also hedges a hot inflation print.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if the trailing stop triggers, if there is a credible US-Iran de-escalation or Hormuz reopening, or if it closes below the 50-day average.

positions.thesis: Defensive health care with a reasonable valuation and an uptrend. It balances energy concentration while breadth is narrow.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on the trailing stop or a close below the 50-day average with weakening relative strength.

positions.thesis: Software is in a strong uptrend, holding up while semis fall. AI demand is moving toward the application layer.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on the trailing stop or if the semis selloff spreads to software, shown by a break of the 50-day average.

positions.thesis: Lower-volatility quality exposure that tends to hold up better if CPI or Fed hike risk hits high-beta stocks.
positions.exit_plan: Swap for higher-conviction momentum if conditions stay calm after CPI.

positions.exit_plan: Sell on the trailing stop or an oil de-escalation catalyst. It would be the first energy position to cut if energy is too heavy.

upcoming_events: Oct 14: September CPI at 8:30 ET. A hot core reading would raise the odds of an October hike and hurt growth stocks.
Oct 14-16: More Q3 bank and big-cap earnings (BAC, MS and others), plus early tech reports.
Oct 15-16: Fed speakers in the run-up to the Oct 27-28 FOMC.
Ongoing: Iran/Hormuz headlines. A strike or de-escalation would move oil and energy ETFs sharply.
Mid-to-late October: Q3 earnings season ramps up, including mega-cap tech late in the month.

sources.title: CNBC: S&P 500 closes near flat, pressured by higher oil prices and memory chip losses
24/7 Wall St: S&P 500 futures pause near record highs as oil rises ahead of bank earnings
Sunday Guardian: Why is the US stock market mixed today (Oct 12)
Schwab: Bracing for busy week: bank earnings, CPI ahead

market_view: The S&P 500 is flat and near record highs, and day-to-day swings are very small. The gains are narrow, though: chip and Asian tech stocks keep falling while energy leads, helped by the Iran conflict and Brent crude near $106. Big banks (Goldman, JPMorgan) posted strong results, but long-term bond yields are high, near 24-year highs, and there is still a chance the Fed raises rates again. With tomorrow's inflation report (CPI) likely to come in hot because of fuel prices, nothing material has changed since this morning's hold decision.
key_drivers: Oct 13: Goldman Sachs beat Q3 estimates as stock-trading revenue jumped 72%. The bank's CEO said a 5% 10-year yield doesn't scare him.
Oct 13: Fed's Waller said AI spending is pushing yields up and that Treasuries no longer carry a safety premium. Fed's Hammack (Oct 12) said more restraint is needed.
Oct 12–13: Brent near $106 with the Iran conflict ongoing; energy (XLE) is at a 20-day high while the Nasdaq and chip stocks slide.
Oct 13: Wells Fargo's CEO warned that the AI buildout is heavily financed with debt; worries about AI funding are hitting Nebius and semiconductors.
Oct 14: September CPI; the headline number is expected hot because of fuel prices.

positions.thesis: Large energy companies benefit from the Iran supply shock and Brent near $106, and the sector has strong momentum. It also hedges the inflation risk in the rest of the portfolio.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if Iran de-escalates or Hormuz reopens and oil breaks down, or if the trailing stop triggers.
positions.plain_reason: Oil companies profit while the Middle East conflict keeps oil prices high.

positions.thesis: Defensive health care in an uptrend that does not depend on AI or rates; it diversifies the leveraged S&P exposure from the idle asset.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if it closes below the 50-day average with a market rotation out of defensives, or if the trailing stop triggers.
positions.plain_reason: Health care companies stay steady even when the economy wobbles.

positions.thesis: Software has strong 60-day momentum, is less exposed to chip-cycle and memory competition worries, and is gaining while semis sell off.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if the AI-funding scare spreads to software, it closes below the 50-day average, or the trailing stop triggers.
positions.plain_reason: Software companies keep growing steadily without needing expensive chip factories.

positions.thesis: Quality stocks with low volatility hold up better if rates and inflation surprise on the upside.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if it breaks below the 50-day average or a better idea needs the money.
positions.plain_reason: Strong, profitable companies tend to hold up better in rough markets.

positions.thesis: Oil and gas producers give more leverage to high crude prices than diversified majors.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on an oil reversal or ceasefire news, or if the trailing stop triggers.
positions.plain_reason: Oil drillers earn more when oil prices stay high.

plain_summary: No changes today: keep holding energy, health care, software and quality stocks ahead of tomorrow's inflation report.
upcoming_events: Oct 14: September CPI. A hot core number would raise the odds of a Fed hike on Oct 27–28.
Oct 14–16: More bank and early tech earnings (BAC, MS, C, etc.), which show how well the economy and lending are holding up.
Oct 16–17: Retail sales and jobless claims, the next read on consumer resilience.
Ongoing: Iran/Hormuz headlines and Fed speakers ahead of the Oct 27–28 FOMC meeting.
